court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, case numbers A386/13 and A289/12
case_name: Mr. Mayank S/O Indramohan Malhotra vs Mrs. Neha Malhotra (Kohli) D/O Ashok
facts_of_case: Petitioner Mayank filed for annulment of marriage under Section 12[1][c] of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Respondent Neha filed for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act. Family Court dismissed the petition and granted restitution with a direction to resume cohabitation.

legal_principles.principle: Fraud must be established by clear and convincing evidence.
legal_principles.held: To explain the concept of fraud as envisaged in Section 12[1][c], he has taken us through judgments reported at AIR 2011 SCW 5763 (Ramesh Kumar and another .vrs. Furu Ram and another) (paragraph no13) and AIR 2014 AP 43 (S. Mahender .vrs. Smt. Shalini).

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging fraud to prove it by clear and convincing evidence.
legal_principles.held: He submits that those photographs have been taken on about 6 different occasions, and hence the entire story of appellant about the disease, its suppression or fraud, is by way of an afterthought.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not lightly annul a marriage on the ground of fraud.
legal_principles.held: He points out that the wife has pointed out physical relationship between the parties in her written statement and though the appellant husband has denied it, fact that he cohabited with the respondent at her parents house at Nagpur between 23.1.2012 to 26.01.2012 is not in dispute.

outcome.final_order: Family Court Appeal No. 73 & 74 of 2015 challenges the dismissal of annulment proceedings filed by him. FCA 74 of 2015 assails the grant of restitution in proceedings filed by Respondent wife.
